paper_metadata.title: Cr-induced morphology change of primary Mn-rich phase in Al-Si-Cu-Mn heat resistant aluminum alloys and its contribution to high temperature strength

evidence.quote: Effect of Cr addition on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Al-12wt.%Si-3.5wt.%Cu-2wt.%Mn heat-resistant alloy were studied by OM , XRD and SEM microstructure observation and tension test at differen t temperature.

attributes.composition: Si/Mn ratio ~2 for slender rods, ~1 for dendrites (at.%)

evidence.quote: In SC0 alloy, without Cr addition, the morphology of primary Mn-rich phase is long dendrites or slender rods (Fig. 1a).
In SC1 alloy , with 0.5wt.%Cr addition, the formation of the slender rods is completely suppressed, and the size of the primary Mn-rich phase dendrites is reduced sharply (Fig. 1b).
When Cr addition is 1.0wt%, the primary Mn-rich phase presents as star-like or particle-like (Fig.1c), and at the same time, the size of it become s smaller.
However, further increasing Cr addition to 1.5wt%, the size of the primary Mn-rich phase become s larger (Fig.1d).
The eutectic Si particles become spherical after solution treatment at 510 oC.
The eutectic Si particles become spherical after solution treatment at 510 oC.
The eutectic CuAl 2 phase, formed during solidification, is found to be partially dissolved into the Al matrix after solutionizing, as shown in the inserted photo at upper right corner of Fig. 2a.

From Fig. 4, it is seen that the peaks of Al, Si, CuAl 2 and Mn-rich phase s still exist after T6 treatment, however, the peak of CuAl 2 phase is weakened considerably or disappeared , consistent with the result in Ref.16.
The peaks corresponding to α -Al, CuAl 2, Si and Mn -rich phases are well consistent with the as -cast XRD results of Al -12wt.%Si-4wt.%Cu-1.2wt.%Mn alloy [16].
